title.narrative: EU Support to Sustainable Energy Connectivity in Central Asia

description.narrative: The overall objective of SECCA is to promote a more sustainable energy mix in the Central Asia region in line with EU best practices. Specifically, the technical assistance programme will work through a range of activities to strengthen public capacity (institutional, human and regulatory, financial), raise awareness, improve data and modelling, improve the identification of bankable projects, and boost regional cooperation, eventually setting the seed for connectivity.

title.narrative: Additional Renewable Energy production by the gridconnected smallscale hydro, solar, wind, and biomass/biogas power plants due to the improved Legal & Regulatory framework and easier access to financing, (MWh)

description.narrative: Additional Renewable Energy production by the gridconnected smallscale hydro, solar, wind, and biomass/biogas power plants due to the improved Legal & Regulatory framework and easier access to financing, (MWh)

comment.narrative: In the baseline scenario REbased electricity generation will be increasing. However this indicator refers to the additional generation due to the improved legal regulatory framework and easier access to financing above the baseline level as a result of SECCA intervention and given that such improvements are not expected in the baseline the baseline level of this indicator equals to zero

The target for this indicator has been established in the following way In Kazakhstan with the most developed RE sector not considering large Hydropower plants in 2020 the total capacity of RE power plants has increased by 585 MW compared with 2019 from 1500 MW to 1635 MW and the electricity production by 844 GWh from 2400.7 GWh to 32401 GWh . However the total capacity of the RE projects selected through the auctions is gradually decreasing in Kazakhstan at the RE auctions 212.89 MW was auctioned in 2019 147.95 MW in 2020 and 86.95 MW in 2021. Therefore considering this and that the total installed capacities of newly built RE smallscale power plants in other CA countries are much smaller assuming that in the baseline scenario the total for all CA countries electricity production of smallscale power plants will increase annually by 500 GWh is a conservative approach. SECCA will facilitate the improvement of the Legal Regulatory framework as well as access to financing. Due to SECCA intervention this number can be increased by 20 i.e. due to SECCA intervention 100 GWh of electricity will be generated annually by the smallscale RE power plants. Therefore by 2026 after 4 years of SECCA implementation 4 100 GWh 400 GWh additional electricity will be generated due to the improved legal regulatory framework and easier access to financing

During the implementation phase since September 2022 SECCA started providing TA for the development of Small Hydropower in Kyrgyzstan. By 14.03.2022 the TA was ongoing and thus its impact is still zero

title.narrative: Number of households switched from fossil fuels for heating to RE, disaggregated by location (urban/rural)

description.narrative: Number of households switched from fossil fuels for heating to RE, disaggregated by location (urban/rural)

comment.narrative: Using RE except biomass for heating is not a common practice in CA especially in large cities where the centralized District Heating DH systems do exist and where the tariffs are quite affordable for most households. Integration of smallscale RE into the heating systems of households as a rule is supported by the State or donors with a heavy grant component. But such programmes have limited funds and timeframes and as a result the impact is also limited. Therefore it is assumed that in the baseline under market conditions there will be no household switched to RE for heating unless they dont have any other alternative. Endofproject Target for 2026 is established based on the assumption that SECCA will promote the legal and regulatory changes for prosumers e.g. households with rooftop solar PV systems especially in rural areas with no DH systems as well as assist the CA countries in creating Financial Support Mechanisms FSM for the financing of such projects.

Biomasstoenergy potential has been estimated in detail for KG and roughly for KZ and UZ. The results have been discussed with stakeholders at the Round Table Assessment of biomass potential for the Kyrgyz Republic held on 17 July 2024. The report on biomass potential assessment for KZ has been submitted to the Ministry of Energy of Kazakhstan. It is expected that the results of asseeements will be considered in the national strategies and action plans.
